findings.problem: The batch shipped 131 em dashes and 23 en dashes, plus 37 arrows, 2 minus signs and the signs for at least, at most, not equal and approximately (U+2190 to U+2BFF, refused by the voice rule in check-home).
findings.fix: Every one rewritten as a comma, colon, full stop or words ("to", "then", "at least", "60% or less", "is not", "about", "minus 7°C"). A node sweep of the batch finds no U+2013, U+2014, U+2212, nothing from U+2190 to U+2BFF, no dash entity and no spaced double hyphen.
findings.source: House rules (the Codex CLAUDE.md and the voice rule in .scripts/check-home.js).

findings.problem: American spellings throughout the Codex's own prose: color, flavor, favorite, labeling, aging (in prose), savory, splendor, polarizing, oxidized, shriveling, toward, apologize, license (noun), chili, program, math, band-aid, nail polish.
findings.fix: British forms: colour, flavour, favourite, labelling, ageing, savoury, splendour, oxidised, shrivelling, towards, apologise, licence, chilli, programme, maths, sticking plaster, nail varnish; goat's cheese. The cat "Wine Trade & Aging" stays byte-identical to the bank.
findings.source: House rule: British spelling; the Codex uses -ise (recognised, oxidised, unpasteurised) and ageing.

findings.problem: "Cafayate's vineyards run to ~3,000 m" put the 3,000 m figure on Cafayate itself, which lies at about 1,700 m; the 3,000 m vineyards are further up the Calchaquí Valleys.
findings.fix: Cafayate at about 1,700 m, with vineyards further up the valley passing 3,000 m; Torrontés Riojano's parentage (Muscat of Alexandria and Criolla Chica) named.
findings.source: Geography of the Calchaquí Valleys (Cafayate about 1,660 to 2,000 m; the highest Salta vineyards above 3,000 m).

findings.problem: "Colchagua and Cachapoal (Apalta)" placed Apalta in Cachapoal; Apalta is in Colchagua, and Cachapoal's Carmenère site is Peumo.
findings.fix: Colchagua (Apalta) and Cachapoal (Peumo); a new trap says both sit inside the Rapel Valley.
findings.source: Chilean DO structure: Rapel holds Cachapoal and Colchagua; Apalta is a Colchagua sector, Peumo a Cachapoal one.

findings.problem: "until 1994 DNA work": the 1994 identification of Carmenère was ampelographic; DNA confirmed it afterwards.
findings.fix: Fact and trap now say ampelography unmasked it in 1994 and DNA confirmed it later.
findings.source: History of the Carmenère identification (field ampelography in 1994, DNA confirmation in 1997).

findings.problem: Chile's legal shape was missing (its regions, the 2011 Costa, Entre Cordilleras and Andes bands, the 75% rule with 85% for the EU), and "Maule/Itata (old-vine País and Carignan)" blurred which grape belongs where.
findings.fix: Chile's geography rewritten north to south by region; a new Chile's signatures row with Maule Carignan (VIGNO), Itata País and Cinsault and the 75%/85% rule.
findings.source: Chilean DO law (Decreto 464 and the 2011 complementary designations); matches the reviewed Regionale Chile chapter.

findings.problem: Argentina beyond Mendoza was absent: Bonarda's identity (Douce Noir, Charbono), a stock Certified question, San Juan, Patagonia and the IP, IG and DOC layers; Malbec's origin as Cahors' Côt unsaid.
findings.fix: New row Argentina beyond Mendoza; Malbec named as the Côt of Cahors; new trap separating Argentine Bonarda (Douce Noir) from Oltrepò Pavese Bonarda (Croatina). No varietal percentage stated for Argentina, which I could not confirm.
findings.source: DNA identification of Argentine Bonarda as Douce Noir; Argentine Ley 25.163 (IP, IG, DOC).

findings.problem: "some pre-phylloxera vines 150+ years" was a misnomer: phylloxera never reached South Australia, so its old vines are own-rooted survivors, not pre-phylloxera relics.
findings.fix: Barossa row now says South Australia kept phylloxera out, vines from the 1840s stand on their own roots, with the Barossa Old Vine Charter grades; a new trap explains the point.
findings.source: South Australian phylloxera quarantine; Barossa Old Vine Charter (Old Vine 35, Survivor 70, Centenarian 100, Ancestor 125 years).

findings.problem: The exam line named GSM blends but no fact covered them, and McLaren Vale was missing.
findings.fix: New row McLaren Vale & GSM (Grenache, Shiraz, Mourvèdre sold as Mataro). Labels row adds the GI ladder (zone, region, subregion) and the descending order of blend names; Coonawarra placed on the Limestone Coast.
findings.source: Australian Wine and Grape Authority labelling and GI rules.

findings.problem: The lead called Central Otago "the world's southernmost serious region"; small Patagonian plantings lie further south, as the fact row's own "near-southernmost" half admitted.
findings.fix: Lead and fact now say "among the southernmost"; a new trap explains the claim.
findings.source: Latitudes: Central Otago about 45°S; Chile Chico (Chile) about 46.5°S and Chubut plantings (Argentina) about 45.6°S.

findings.problem: "~95%+ screwcapped since the early 2000s" stated a volatile statistic as fact.
findings.fix: Now dated to the New Zealand Screwcap Wine Seal Initiative of 2001, with screwcap sealing "the great majority"; the 85% labelling rule added.
findings.source: House rule: nothing volatile stated as fact.

findings.problem: The thiol trap was muddled ("cat pee/boxwood is thiols at high level, describe as passionfruit/boxwood"): passionfruit and boxwood are thiols, green pepper and cut grass are methoxypyrazines.
findings.fix: Trap now assigns each note to its compound family.
findings.source: Sauvignon Blanc aroma chemistry (3MH, 3MHA and 4MMP thiols; IBMP methoxypyrazine).

findings.problem: Only five regions were named; Gisborne, Nelson and North Canterbury with Waipara, all asked, were missing, as were Marlborough's Southern Valleys and the 1973 planting.
findings.fix: New row The rest of the map; Marlborough row adds the Southern Valleys and Montana's 1973 planting.
findings.source: New Zealand Winegrowers regional map.

findings.problem: Constantia was called "a legend of the 18th century (Napoleon's exile pour)": Napoleon's exile on St Helena was 1815 to 1821, in the 19th century.
findings.fix: Now "a legend of the 18th and 19th centuries, shipped to Napoleon in exile on St Helena"; Klein Constantia's revival dated to 1986.
findings.source: Napoleon's exile dates; Klein Constantia's first Vin de Constance, 1986.

findings.problem: "Eben Sadie's Columella/Palladius" named a living person as the current winemaker and owner, a volatile fact.
findings.fix: Now "The Sadie Family's Columella and Palladius", the winery's name.
findings.source: House rule: no living person named as a volatile fact.

findings.problem: The lead's "350-year-old industry" understated it (first wine 1659), and the WO row's "world's oldest sustainability seal" was an unverifiable claim; the WO ladder, Cap Classique and the 85% vintage rule were missing.
findings.fix: Lead "Wine since 1659"; the WO row now gives the ladder (geographical unit, region, district, ward), 85% for variety or vintage, the neck seal certifying the claims and, since 2010, sustainability, and Cap Classique. The Old Vine Project seal (35 years and more) added to Chenin.
findings.source: Wine and Spirit Board WO scheme; Integrity and Sustainability seal (2010); Old Vine Project Certified Heritage Vineyards.

findings.problem: Pinotage called "the base of the Cape Blend"; a Cape Blend has no legal definition and Pinotage is a component, not necessarily the base.
findings.fix: Now "a common part of a Cape Blend".
findings.source: Wines of South Africa usage of the term.

findings.problem: Franciacorta "Satèn & Millesimato 24+" was wrong for Millesimato, which needs 30 months on the lees; Rosé (24) was missing.
findings.fix: Franciacorta 18 months on the lees, Satèn and Rosé 24, Millesimato 30, Riserva 60.
findings.source: Franciacorta DOCG disciplinare.

findings.problem: The Cava minimums ignored the 2020 reform that created Cava de Guarda and Cava de Guarda Superior (Reserva, Gran Reserva, Paraje Calificado).
findings.fix: Minimums row now names Cava de Guarda 9 months and Cava de Guarda Superior, created in 2020, with Reserva 18, Gran Reserva 30 and Paraje Calificado 36.
findings.source: Consejo Regulador del Cava, 2020 regulation.

findings.problem: Prosecco was given one DOCG, "Valdobbiadene-Conegliano" (the name runs Conegliano Valdobbiadene, and Asolo is a second DOCG), the trap said the DOCG "still uses tank method" without exception, and Prosecco DOC Rosé (2020) was missing.
findings.fix: New row Prosecco's map (both DOCGs, Cartizze and the Rive, DOC Rosé with 10 to 15% Pinot Nero and a vintage); trap now "Most Prosecco, DOCG included, is made in tank".
findings.source: Prosecco DOC and DOCG disciplinari; Prosecco DOC Rosé approved in 2020.

findings.problem: Crémant's "9 to 12 months minimum lees" blurred two rules, and the sweetness scale, a staple label question, was absent.
findings.fix: Crémant: at least 9 months on the lees and 12 before release. New row Sweetness words (Brut Nature to Doux in g/L) and a trap that Extra Dry is sweeter than Brut. Ancestral row names the AOCs that keep the method.
findings.source: Crémant AOC rules; EU sparkling sweetness terms (Reg. 2019/33).

findings.problem: Solera: "draw from the oldest criadera, refresh from younger" misnamed the tiers; wine is drawn from the solera itself, and the criaderas are the younger tiers that refill it.
findings.fix: Now drawn from the oldest tier (the solera), refilled from the first criadera, that from the next.
findings.source: Sherry solera terminology (solera, primera criadera, saca, rocío).

findings.problem: Nothing reflected the Sherry rules agreed in 2021: Fino and Manzanilla need no fortifying if they reach 15% naturally, and ageing may take place across the Marco de Jerez (Manzanilla still only in Sanlúcar).
findings.fix: Added to Sherry, biological; the lead keeps "wine plus spirit" as the general picture.
findings.source: WebSearch: Decanter, sherry.wine and The Drinks Business on the 2021 reform.

findings.problem: Port's grapes, Douro schist, strength, Vila Nova de Gaia, Colheita's seven years, Single Quinta, white and rosé Port were missing; Madeira lacked its age words and Terrantez; the VDN row did not split white Muscat from red Grenache, and Topaque and the Rutherglen ladder names were absent; Marsala was missing.
findings.fix: Port split into Port (place, grapes, aguardente, 19 to 22%) and Port styles; Madeira age words added; VDN row split by colour with Rasteau and Frontignan; Rutherglen, Classic, Grand, Rare; new Other fortified row (Marsala, Moscatel de Setúbal); a Colheita trap; Pale Cream added.
findings.source: IVDP categories; IVBAM Madeira categories; Rutherglen Muscat classification; Marsala DOC.

findings.problem: The exam line named the German Prädikat sweet tiers, but no fact row covered them; Sauternes and Barsac and Tokaji's post-2013 rules were also missing.
findings.fix: New rows German & Austrian tiers (Auslese to Trockenbeerenauslese, Ausbruch, Strohwein), Sauternes & Barsac (five communes, the Ciron, Yquem's 1855 rank) and Tokaji (120 g/L since 2013, puttonyos 5 or 6, Eszencia 450 g/L, Szamorodni); a Barsac trap.
findings.source: German Weingesetz; Tokaj wine law 2013; 1855 classification.

findings.problem: "5.5% alcohol is the tell" for Moscato d'Asti gave one figure where the DOCG allows a range of about 4.5 to 6.5% actual alcohol.
findings.fix: Now "its low alcohol, about 5 to 6%, is the tell".
findings.source: Asti DOCG disciplinare.

findings.problem: Albariza was filed under chalk and called "diatomaceous chalk"; it is a white calcareous marl rich in diatoms, not true chalk.
findings.fix: Listed as "a white marl rich in diatoms"; trap now "a dazzling white marl of chalk and diatoms" that soaks up winter rain.
findings.source: Jerez soil science (albariza: calcium carbonate, clay and diatom silica).

findings.problem: "Mosel's 60°+ south faces" gave a gradient that confuses degrees with per cent and cannot be stood on as stated.
findings.fix: Now "the Mosel's steep south-facing slate".
findings.source: Calmont and other Mosel slopes are usually quoted in per cent; the degree figure is unsafe.

findings.problem: Missing material a candidate is asked: growing degree days and the Winkler regions, Left Bank gravel against Right Bank clay, galestro and alberese, loess, Douro schist; Kimmeridgian omitted Sancerre.
findings.fix: New rows Measuring heat and Gravel & clay; schist and the Tuscan and Austrian soil names added; Sancerre added; a trap separates Kimmeridgian (Chablis, Sancerre, the Aube) from the Côte des Blancs' chalk.
findings.source: Amerine and Winkler (UC Davis); standard soil teaching.

findings.problem: Tequila was placed in Jalisco only; the denomination also covers named municipalities of Guanajuato, Michoacán, Nayarit and Tamaulipas. Extra Añejo was missing.
findings.fix: Now "from Jalisco and named parts of four other states"; Extra Añejo (3 years and more) added.
findings.source: NOM-006-SCFI tequila standard.

findings.problem: Gaps: the six Cognac crus and Fine Champagne, Armagnac's three areas, Scotch's 40% minimum and the islands within Highland, bourbon's proof limits and "straight", grappa, pisco and vermouth; Manhattan given as rye only.
findings.fix: Brandy split into Cognac and Armagnac & Calvados; whisky rows extended; new row Pomace, pisco & vermouth; Manhattan "rye or bourbon"; trap that bourbon need not come from Kentucky.
findings.source: Cognac and Armagnac AOC rules; Scotch Whisky Regulations 2009; US 27 CFR 5.22.

findings.problem: "Trappist is a legal designation" and "brewed IN the monastery" overstated both: Trappist is a protected label of the International Trappist Association, for beer brewed within or near the abbey under the monks' oversight.
findings.fix: Belgium row and trap rewritten accordingly.
findings.source: International Trappist Association criteria for the Authentic Trappist Product label.

findings.problem: "a Certified somm" named the CMS level where the Codex names its levels Regionale, Village, Premier Cru and Grand Cru.
findings.fix: Now "a sommelier".
findings.source: House rule on level names.

findings.problem: Missing: the four ingredients, IBU and the Reinheitsgebot; cider's AOPs and perry. "Pommeau and Calvados upstream" had the direction wrong; both are made from cider apples, alongside or after.
findings.fix: New row Four ingredients; cider row adds AOP Pays d'Auge, Cornouaille and Poiré Domfront, with Pommeau and Calvados "alongside"; a Kölsch hybrid trap.
findings.source: Reinheitsgebot (Bavaria, 1516); French cider AOPs.

findings.problem: "Junmai/Honjozo: ~70%" gave Junmai a polishing requirement it has not had since 2004 (it must only state its ratio); Honjozo is 70% or less.
findings.fix: Polish ladder now gives Honjozo 70% or less and Junmai no minimum since 2004, ratio stated.
findings.source: National Tax Agency labelling standard for special-designation sake (2004 revision).

findings.problem: "multiple parallel fermentation, unique to sake" overclaimed (huangjiu and makgeolli use it too); "~15 to 17% alcohol" ignored undiluted strength; the trap "a misnomer twice over" did not say why; the sake meter value, Kimoto and Yamahai, Tokubetsu and the 10% alcohol cap were missing.
findings.fix: "The defining technique"; 18 to 20% undiluted, usually 15 to 16%; trap explains that wine is fermented fruit; new row Reading the label (Nihonshu-do), style terms extended; a trap that plus means drier.
findings.source: National Tax Agency standards; standard sake teaching.

findings.problem: The deductive tasting grid, the heart of the Certified tasting, had no row; red and white fermentation differences were thin.
findings.fix: New row The tasting grid (sight, nose, palate, conclusion) in the Codex's own words; Colour row adds warm red and cooler white fermentation; "BOS chapter" spelled out as the Business of the Sommelier chapter; Gewurz written in full.
findings.source: Standard deductive tasting method.

findings.problem: Germany's row ignored the 2021 wine law's origin pyramid (growing region, region, Ortswein, Lagenwein), binding from the 2026 vintage.
findings.fix: Added beside the Prädikat ladder (now spelled out), with the VDP pyramid named as its model.
findings.source: WebSearch: German wine law reform of January 2021, transition to the 2026 vintage (several trade sources agree).

findings.problem: Italy's "pink strip on the neck" stated one colour for the DOCG seal, which is not uniform; Spain lacked Vino de Pago and the Rioja ageing figures; the US line lacked county, state and California rules and the 85% vintage rule without an AVA; "Chile/Argentina: 75 to 85% rules" was vague; "five dialects of cru" counted châteaux twice.
findings.fix: Numbered government neck strip; Vino de Pago and Rioja Crianza, Reserva, Gran Reserva figures; US rules completed; Chile 75%, 85% for the EU; South Africa joins the 85% list; the cru sentence lists vineyard, village and château meanings without a count.
findings.source: 27 CFR 4.25 and 4.27; Rioja DOCa ageing rules; Chilean DO law.

findings.problem: Clarification and stability (sulphur dioxide, fining and vegan wine, tartrate crystals), a stock service question, was missing, as were training systems and the 228 litre pièce; phylloxera's escapees listed "some Barossa" where all of South Australia escaped; carbonic maceration credited to Beaujolais where semi-carbonic is the norm.
findings.fix: New row Clarity & stability; training systems and barrel sizes added; "some Barossa" widened to South Australia as a whole, plus sandy soils; "Beaujolais's semi-carbonic wines"; 17 g/L of sugar per 1% alcohol added.
findings.source: Standard oenology; South Australian phylloxera quarantine.

findings.problem: The formats row said the magnum "ages slowest per volume" (larger formats age more slowly still) and gave "Jeroboam, Imperial 6L" without noting that the Jeroboam is 3 litres in Champagne and 5 in Bordeaux.
findings.fix: Formats row gives the Champagne ladder to Nebuchadnezzar and the Bordeaux double magnum, Jeroboam and Imperial; the magnum "ages more slowly than a bottle".
findings.source: Standard bottle-size tables.

findings.problem: The trap ended "American law, not world" followed by the retired study word.
findings.fix: Now "American law, not a worldwide rule".
findings.source: House rule: the retired study word is never used, in either spelling.

findings.problem: "Fluctuation worse than either" ranked temperature swings above heat and light, an overstatement; auction vocabulary stopped at a bare "ullage".
findings.fix: Now "wide swings in temperature do damage of their own"; new row Auction talk (into the neck, top shoulder, mid shoulder, OWC, ex-château); Diam written as a name.
findings.source: Standard cellaring guidance.

findings.problem: The exam line named glassware logic, but no row covered glassware or the order of wines.
findings.fix: New row Glasses & order (polish, stem, placing, flute and bowl; white before red, light before full, dry before sweet, young before old).
findings.source: Standard floor service.

findings.problem: "women first where practical" stated an order many houses no longer use; the pour sum "a table of eight needs two bottles" held only at a full 5 oz pour; temperatures were in Fahrenheit only.
findings.fix: Sequence now notes the tradition and the plain clockwise alternative; pour row gives both the full-pour and 3 oz cases; Celsius added to every temperature.
findings.source: Current floor service teaching varies by house; arithmetic.

findings.problem: The lead's "salt against tannin's enemies and bitter against nothing" did not make sense aloud, and the rule of pairing to the sauce or dominant element was missing.
findings.fix: Lead rewritten; new row Pair the strongest element.
findings.source: Standard pairing principles.

findings.problem: "by-the-glass programs run richer cost %" was backwards: under the first-glass rule a glass runs at a 20% cost, lower than a bottle, to cover the waste of open bottles.
findings.fix: Glass maths now gives the 20% cost and says why by-the-glass wines carry the lower percentage.
findings.source: Arithmetic: one glass of five priced at the bottle's cost gives 1/5 = 20%.

findings.problem: The cost of goods formula, the basis of any inventory question, was missing; "Wine keys POS-mapped" garbled the point (a wine key is a corkscrew); "healthy lists turn 4 to 8×" was an unsourced benchmark stated as fact.
findings.fix: New row Cost of goods (opening plus purchases minus closing); Programme hygiene now "every wine keyed correctly into the point-of-sale system"; turnover described as "several times a year"; the markup trap now gives the 67% margin.
findings.source: Standard beverage cost accounting.
